cards.text: This is the LORD's word through the prophet Zechariah (Zechariah 1:1), and it's about Jerusalem. The LORD says, "Behold, a day of the LORD is coming when your plunder will be divided in your presence." Then He says He will gather all the nations for battle against Jerusalem.

cards.question: All the nations come for battle against Jerusalem. What happens to the city?

cards.text: The houses are looted, and the women ravished. Then the LORD tells what happens to the people of the city.

cards.question: When Jerusalem is captured, every last person in the city is carried off into exile.

cards.text: Half the city goes into exile, but the rest of the people stay in the city. And then somebody goes out to fight against those nations.

cards.question: Who goes out to fight against the nations that came against Jerusalem?

cards.text: And here's where it gets BIG, friend. On that day His feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem.

cards.question: When the LORD's feet stand on the Mount of Olives, what happens to the mountain?

cards.text: It splits from east to west into a great valley, half the mountain moving north and half moving south. Friend, I can't break ONE cookie in half without crumbs going everywhere, and the LORD splits a MOUNTAIN.

cards.question: Jerusalem is under attack, and a brand new valley just opened up, reaching all the way to Azal. The LORD says you will ___ by His mountain valley.

cards.text: You'll flee the way you fled from the earthquake in the days of Uzziah, king of Judah. Then the prophet says the LORD his God will come, and He's not coming alone.

cards.question: The prophet says the LORD his God will come. Who comes with Him?

cards.text: On that day there will be no light, no cold or frost, a unique day known only to the LORD, without day or night. Don't look at me for the date, friend: I spent YEARS in a junk drawer not even knowing what day it WAS.

cards.question: On that unique day, when evening comes, it gets dark like any other evening.

cards.text: And on that day living water will flow out from Jerusalem. This chapter just keeps going, friend.

cards.question: Where does the living water flowing out from Jerusalem go?
The living water from Jerusalem flows in summer and winter alike.

cards.text: Now here comes the line I'd frame and hang over every oven in my bakery. It's about who rules over all the earth.

cards.question: On that day the LORD will become ___ over all the earth.

cards.text: It's "the LORD alone, and His name alone." King over ALL the earth, and me? I'm in charge of one little cookie planet, and my oven STILL doesn't listen to me.

All the land from Geba to Rimmon, south of Jerusalem, turns into a plain, but Jerusalem is raised up and stays in her place, from gate to gate and tower to winepresses. The land south of it goes flat and Jerusalem RISES, like the one cookie in my batch that actually puffs up right.

cards.question: Even after being raised up, Jerusalem will face utter destruction again someday.

cards.text: People will live there, and Jerusalem will dwell securely. Then the LORD turns to the peoples who warred against Jerusalem, and He strikes them with a plague.

cards.question: What does the LORD's plague do to the peoples who warred against Jerusalem?

answers.text: Their flesh rots as they stand
Their cities fall into the sea

cards.text: On that day a great panic from the LORD comes upon them.

cards.question: When a great panic from the LORD comes on the peoples who warred against Jerusalem, what do they do?

cards.text: Judah will also fight at Jerusalem. Now remember how this chapter started, with Jerusalem's plunder divided right in front of them?

cards.question: Judah fights at Jerusalem. What happens to the wealth of all the surrounding nations?

answers.text: It is collected in great abundance
It is scattered across the land
It is all sent back home

cards.text: A similar plague strikes the horses, mules, camels and donkeys in those camps. Then comes a turn I did NOT see coming, and it's about the survivors from those same nations.

cards.question: What will the survivors from the nations that came against Jerusalem do year after year?

answers.text: Go up to worship the King

cards.question: Year after year, the survivors go up to worship the King, the LORD of Hosts. Which feast do they come to celebrate?

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks about any families of the earth that don't go up to Jerusalem to worship the King.

cards.question: If any families of the earth don't go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, then the ___ will not fall on them.

cards.text: Then the LORD names one nation in particular: Egypt.

cards.question: If the people of Egypt don't go up to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles, the rain will still fall on them.

cards.text: This will be the punishment of Egypt and of all the nations that don't go up. Then, on that day, even ordinary things are set apart for the LORD, starting with words inscribed on the bells of the horses.

cards.question: On that day, ___ TO THE LORD will be inscribed on the bells of the horses.

cards.text: The cooking pots in the house of the LORD will be like the sprinkling bowls before the altar, and every pot in Jerusalem and Judah will be holy to the LORD of Hosts. EVERY POT, friend, and I thought going from a 25-cent bin to a gold base was a big glow-up.
All who sacrifice will come and take some of those pots and cook in them. Holy bells, holy pots, and one last change in the house of the LORD of Hosts, about the Canaanites.

cards.question: On that day, there will no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the LORD of Hosts.

findings.problem: The joke says "the LORD splits a MOUNTAIN." Zechariah 14:4 says the LORD's feet will stand on the Mount of Olives and that the mountain "will be split in two." It never says the LORD splits it. The joke turns a link the text leaves open into a stated fact about what God does.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "This chapter just keeps going, friend" can read as a complaint about how long the Scripture is, not as wonder. It also adds nothing to the moment.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: The question asks what the plague does to the peoples. Only the right answer is about the people themselves. The wrong answers are about their land and their cities, so the right answer stands out as the only one that fits a plague striking peoples.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: "Now remember how this chapter started, with Jerusalem's plunder divided right in front of them?" sets up verse 14 as a reversal of verse 1. The text never links Judah collecting the nations' wealth to Jerusalem's plunder in verse 1.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "Then the LORD speaks about any families of the earth..." names the LORD as the speaker. Zechariah 14:17 refers to "the King, the LORD of Hosts" in the third person and doesn't say who is speaking. Card 14 does the same with "Then the LORD names one nation in particular," for verse 18, which also refers to "the LORD" in the third person.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The blank is for what will not fall on those who don't go up, and it is a punishment. "Fire" and "sword" not falling on them would be a mercy, so neither wrong answer is believable, and "rain" is the only answer that works.

rule.text: Wrong answers for what someone does or says only need to be believable.

findings.problem: The joke calls back to "a 25-cent bin." Nothing earlier in this lesson sets that up, and onboarding only covers the junk drawer. A baker may not catch the reference.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: "One last change in the house of the LORD of Hosts, about the Canaanites" gives away the true or false on card 20. Calling it a change about the Canaanites tells the baker that the statement "there will no longer be a Canaanite" is true.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Many cards retell the prophecy in the present tense, as if it is happening now ("Half the city goes into exile," "It splits from east to west," "a great panic from the LORD comes upon them," "A similar plague strikes"). Other cards keep the text's future "will." The tenses switch back and forth across the walkthrough.
findings.question: Can prophetic passages be retold in the storyteller's present tense, or should Papa Dorin keep the text's future tense ("will") for predicted events, so the baker never takes a prophecy as something that already happened or is being predicted by him?
